messages.subject: Re: CHM
messages.body_plain:
HI,

You were right. The problem was that because my drone is not RTK and i haven't used GCPs, my Z scale between my 2 DSM was not the same. So i have substract the difference from all the plots results at the end, and the correlation with manual measure is really good. I will use GPCs in the future trials.

Thx a lot !

Tony

Le jeudi 23 septembre 2021 à 15:17:02 UTC+2, fmatias a écrit :
>
> Hi Tony,
>
>
>
> To evaluate plant height on small plots it is very important to have a more precise GIS correction or geometric calibration to avoid weird results. For example, using GCPs or having RTK-GPS on the drone. Please, take the time to look at this example: https://filipematias23.github.io/FIELDimageR-Workshop-10/#example-02
>
>
>
> In this example, I was working with an orthomosaic with no geometric calibration. My intention was to evaluate plat height for different populations of potatoes (from left to right are T1, T2, T3, and T4). In the image below, I plotted the value extracted per plot for all trials. Apparently, seems that T1 (bluer) is at least 1 meter taller than T4 (redder), but that is not true. It happens because I extracted the data without removing the soil base. What we are seeing is the effect of slope in the terrain.
>
>
>
>
>
> Trying to adapt to your case, maybe because you didn’t correct the geographic position between your soil base and the orthomosaic with plants, the alignment of plots is not good generating a bad calculation of the canopy height model (CHM). One possible solution is using instead the DEM from soil base flight will be to use the Digital Terrain Model (DTM) from the same orthomosaic with plants. In other words, the idea is to use the CHM=DEM-DTM from the same flight. Is that make sense? For future evaluations of plant height think about using GCPs… ok
>
>
>
> Hope that helps…!!!
>
>
>
> All the best,
>
> Filipe

messages.subject: Masking by height from CHM
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Is it possible to create a mask using the CHM instead of VI's? I'm analyzing trees in pasture and the VI's are not distinct enough to segment out the trees but the CHM is very defined. I would like to mask out all values under .25 meter from the CHM and use that as the mask for fieldMask.

Thanks,

Eric
